and is a path no keystroke takes. Driving the same triggers through
execCommand('insertText') converts zero of six before this change and ten of
ten after.

Normalised for the TEST only. The model keeps whatever the browser put there:
rewriting the author's text so a pattern matches would be a worse cure than the
disease.

Found by an agent building code highlighting, which needed the same trailing
space for its ```lang fence.

* spaces: an icon name from a mailed file must not resolve through the prototype

'toString' in ICONS is true and resolves to a function, so a page whose icon is
"toString" or "constructor" returned native source text and skipped the escape
on the line below. It stringifies to text rather than markup, so this was not
an injection — but it is author-supplied data reaching the page unescaped, and
the next lookup table indexed with `in` might not be so lucky.

Found by an agent building callouts, which needed the same lookup for tone
icons.

* spaces: the starter space must not teach a trigger that no longer fires

Every other hint in the starter shows its trailing space explicitly — '[] ',
'> ' — because that space is part of the trigger. The two code-fence hints did
not, and the fence is exactly where it now matters: the rule grew a language
capture this round, so typing ``` alone stopped converting and only ``` plus a
space does.

The starter space is the first thing anyone sees and the only documentation
most people will read. An instruction in it that does not work is worse than no
instruction.

* spaces: the duplicated lists four parallel agents each recreated

Four features merged in a day, built by agents who could not see each other's
work, and each needed something the codebase already knew. Two copies got in:

model.ts gained KNOWN_BLOCK_TYPES beside the block registry, and agent.ts
restated the sanitizer's unwrap policy as a lowercased literal. Both were
correct on arrival, which is exactly what makes them dangerous — a copy is
right until the original changes, and then it is wrong in a way nothing
reports. validate() reporting a real block type as unknown would have an agent
'fix' a working document.

Both now derive: known types from SPECS, the unwrap set from the sanitizer's
exported UNWRAP. Pinned by assertions whose negative controls fire.

Also: the sanitizer's UNWRAP is exported rather than duplicated, because
validate() genuinely needs to tell an agent which block-level tags get
unwrapped out of inline html.

* spaces: five defects an adversarial review reproduced, and four claims of mine that were not true

Every one of these shipped with all gates green. Each lived in a case the
author's own spot-check did not reach, which is the argument for the review.

THE DEFECTS

1. Markdown export broke the GitHub alert and the fence whenever a callout
   child spanned more than one line. about.ts prefixed '> ' per returned
   ELEMENT, but an element can hold newlines — a code block's body is one
   multi-line string, and htmlToMd turns <br> into a newline. The 2nd line
   carried no '>', which ends the blockquote, unterminates the fence and drops
   the rest of the callout out of the box as broken prose. Quoted per line now,
   with a bare '>' for blank lines because a truly blank line closes the quote.

2. Markdown import double-escaped the visible text of every link, wikilink,
   autolink and image alt: '[Q&A](…)' reached the file as 'Q&amp;A' and the
   reader saw the entity. Display text is not escaped at those four sites any
   more — the single esc() at the end does it once, as it always did for
   ordinary prose. Bold, italic and code were never affected because their text
   sits outside a placeholder, which is exactly why a spot-check of "inline
   formatting survived" passed.

3. bento.updatePage(id, {parent}) hung the tab forever on a page cycle. parseDoc
   preserves A.parent=B/B.parent=A (it only drops parents naming no page), so
   the cycle arrives from any mailed file, and the ancestor walk had no visited
   set. Measured: the call never returns, exit 124. The reachable sequence is
   the RECOMMENDED one — validate() reports the cycle, an agent re-homes a page
   to fix it, and that call kills the tab with every unsaved edit in it.

4. Markdown import created pages with zero blocks — one per folder without a
   folder note, one per empty file, plus the invented root — and then navigated
   to one of them. A zero-block page has no editable host, no gutter and no /
   menu, so the first thing a vault import showed you was a page you could not
   put a caret in, permanently.

5. A list item holding an image, followed by a continuation line, wrote the
   literal string "undefined" into the document and hid the author's prose. An
   image has no html and is not a container, so it is now neither a
   continuation target nor a parent: the line becomes its own paragraph beside
   the image rather than a child of it.

THE CLAIMS

- 'the ceiling is checked per feature from here' (DECISIONS.md, yesterday) was
  written with NO MECHANISM behind it, and the breach was found by a reviewer
  reading the number rather than by a build failing. scripts/test-spaces-size.mjs
  and size-budgets.json exist now and CI runs them. Raising a ceiling stays
  expected; raising it silently is what the check stops.
- 'exports as a GitHub alert with its nested blocks intact' was true only for
  the three single-line children I tried. Corrected in the changelog.
- 'A page is never left with zero blocks' was measured against the EDITOR,
  which still cannot produce one. The importer landed in the same tree and did.
  An invariant proved for one writer is not proved for the next.
- 'Containers are registry data rather than a b.type === "toggle" test' — one
  such test survived in revealBlock, latent only while toggle is the sole fold
  type. A ⌘K hit inside the second one would have landed on a hidden block.

Shell 108,271 B against a 112,640 B ceiling. 284 rig checks; the new
assertions' negative controls fire, and the cycle guard is checked structurally
as well as behaviourally so a regression FAILS rather than hanging CI.

* spaces: look like the suite it belongs to

Four things a person opening both apps would notice, and all four were real:

The SPLASH was plain white text while slides has the animated bento mark on a
dark radial field. Ported verbatim from slides/index.html — markup and CSS —
rather than reimplemented, so the two cannot drift.

The WORDMARK was decoration. It is the suite's mark now, and it opens About —
which previously had no route to it except a ⋯ menu nobody opens. On a narrow
screen it keeps the mark and drops the word, as slides does. About itself now
opens with the same head slides uses: mark, app, version, and a link back to
bento.page. A dialog that opens on a section heading does not say what you are
looking at.

SAVE was two adjacent buttons; it is one control with two fused halves, and it
carries the amber unsaved dot — the place you look to find out whether you need
to press it is the button itself. That needed a real dirty flag: store.ts has
claimed since 0.1.0 that the typing run sets 'the dirty flag', and there was no
such flag. It also needed the clean-to-dirty TRANSITION to emit, because a
typing run deliberately does not emit per keystroke — without that the dot
appeared 600ms after you started typing and the button lied until then.

UNDO/REDO were scattered: redo sat in the overflow menu while undo was inline.
They are one group beside the document's identity now, matching slides' LEFT =
the document / RIGHT = what you do with it. The title input no longer eats the
slack, which is what had pushed them into the middle of the bar.

Not addressed, because it does not exist: collaboration. Spaces has no Live
button because it has no live session — that is an eleven-step project whose
first step (the byte-equivalence rig) is in this branch. A button that opened
an empty People panel would be worse than its absence.

Shell 108,271 → 109,455 B, within the 112,640 B ceiling. Five new strings, all
eight catalogs.

* spaces: the page list resizes and collapses, and undo/redo are the suite's

Two things that still did not match bento/slides.

UNDO/REDO used circular arrows — the shape every app uses for 'reload'. They
are slides' glyphs now, character for character, because a control that
promises the wrong thing is worse than an ugly one.

THE PAGE LIST was a fixed 244px column with its only control in the toolbar.
It now behaves as slides' panels do: a 5px strip between the panel and the
page, drag to resize (clamped 150–420, verified at both ends), double-click to
reset, and a chevron tab ON the strip that collapses it to nothing and then
docks flush to the screen edge so there is always a way back.  toggles it.
The width and the collapsed state are the READER's, so they live in
localStorage and never touch the document — the same rule as language.

The chevron is visible without hovering. My first version faded it in on
:hover, which meant the way to hide the panel was invisible until you happened
to pass over a five-pixel strip; slides' is a permanent white pill and it is
right. The rig now refuses an opacity:0 default.

Below 820px the panel stays a DRAWER rather than becoming a 0px column — on a
phone the page needs the whole width, and a column collapsed to nothing would
leave nothing to reopen it from.

The size gate added yesterday earned its place immediately: this work went 1,370 B
over the 110 KiB ceiling and the build said so. Raised to 114 KiB here, in the
commit that spends it, with the reason in size-budgets.json — which is exactly
the discipline the gate exists to enforce, and the opposite of what happened
when the 100 KiB ceiling was passed silently.

* spaces: the review's remaining items, and a crash the last one uncovered

THE PAGES BUTTON. Retired above the drawer breakpoint. The panel now has a
chevron on its own edge, where you are already looking, so a second control for
the same thing sat to the LEFT of the wordmark and pushed the suite's mark out
of the corner every app in the suite puts it in. Slides has no topbar panel
toggle for exactly this reason. Below 820px there is no strip to hang a chevron
on, so the button is the only way in and it leads the bar.

Then the review list:

- Reading view is read-only again: the callout tone chip had no guard, so a
  click in reading view committed a tone change — undo entry, dirty flag and
  all — while the renderer was deliberately emitting an inert span beside it.
- Tab now NESTS. It always wrote `parent`; nothing rendered it, because only
  registry containers opened a body, so an indented bullet came out flat and
  Tab was a key that did nothing you could see. A list item hosts its own
  children now: verified three levels deep, with a numbered child under a
  bullet rendering as a nested <ol> and the following paragraph not swallowed.
  Fixing the renderer rather than the starter copy, because the copy was right.
- validate() no longer calls a LEGAL block anchor a broken link. It looked up
  the whole `#p/<page>/<block>` remainder as a page id and reported severity
  ERROR with a fix ("remove the link") that would have destroyed a working
  link. It uses the same last-slash rule as the resolver and the backlink index.
- Asset keys go through Object.hasOwn: `assets['toString']` returned a function,
  which is truthy, so the `?? ''` never fired and a stringified function was
  assigned to img.src.
- The tone and language popovers were keyboard traps — they set this.overlay,
  onKey early-returns on it, and neither took focus or listened for Escape.
- Print no longer puts a live "Load this image" button on paper.
- planUpdateBlock runs the registry's init on a type change, so an agent-written
  callout has a tone and an agent-written to-do has `done`.
- bento.search reads textOf(), not tag-stripped html: entities are decoded, so
  it stops missing text the reader can see and matching text that is not there.
- Duplicate note names are reported on import. First one wins — the only thing
  a bare [[name]] can mean — but silently every link to the second went to the
  first, including that note's links to itself, and the summary claimed success.
- KnownBlockType is gone. It was unused, hand-maintained, and its comment
  described a runtime list that no longer exists.

THE SYNC RIG, and what it found. Its canon is built by DELETING volatile keys
from toJSON() rather than listing six stable ones — the listed version would
have been blind to any seventh field, including one added by the very
parameterization the rig exists to check. Its mutants now survive a fromJSON
round trip (crdt.ts's static fromJSON constructs `new SyncState` literally, so
scenarios that restore state were testing the baseline against itself while
reporting mutant coverage).

And the generator was taught to REMOVE a property, which it had never done.
That immediately crashed the shipped engine: replayStash carries the identical
JSON.stringify(undefined).slice defect that was fixed at the `set` site months
ago — the fix went where the bug was found rather than everywhere the pattern
was, and the rig covered the found site only. Reached whenever a removal is
parked during a node's dead window and replayed on resurrection. One line, in
slides/src/sync/crdt.ts.

That site is NOT pinned by a hand-written case, and the comment in
test-crdt-delprop.ts says so: two constructed scenarios failed to reach it and
passed with the fix reverted, which is worse than no test. The guard is the
generator — measured, test-sync.ts throws with the fix reverted and passes
45,688 checks with it.

* spaces: a saved space shows its content to readers that run no script

Reported from the field: the file opened to the boot splash and stayed there.

The cause is not the splash. The runtime ships DEFLATED and is inflated by a
loader at boot, so where scripting is off nothing inflates, nothing boots, and
nothing ever removes the splash — the file shows a loading animation where its
content should be. That is what macOS QuickLook, iOS Files, Bento Tray and any
HTML preview pane see of every space saved so far. It only surfaced now because
the splash became a full dark animation this week; the plain white one looked
like a slow load rather than a hang.

Slides solved this in 0.9.x and spaces never called the mechanism: every save
now writes a still render of the home page into the shell, followed IMMEDIATELY
by a parser-blocking script that deletes both. A thumbnailer keeps it — it runs
no script; a reader never sees it — the remover runs before the first paint.
The shell gate already asserts that ordering for preview-carrying shells.

Verified on a real save: 3,513 bytes of preview (budget 64KB), the host
followed directly by the remover and both ahead of #app, and the preview's
z-index above the splash's so it covers it rather than hiding behind it.
Rendered, it is the page — headings, prose, lists, links, and to-do state as ☐/☑
glyphs, since an <input> is a control and a still has none.

Two rules it inherits and one it adds. Inherited: an encrypted space never
carries a preview (plaintext beside ciphertext is the leak the password
exists to prevent), and the preview REPLACES rather than appends. Added: the
still may not FETCH — href and non-data src are stripped, so a remote image
cannot phone home from a file manager, which is the remote-image consent rule
applied where nobody could consent.

It has its own stylesheet rather than reusing the app's, because the app's
ships deflated too and does not exist in this mode.

bento/dash is now a Bento file. 25 KB compressed shell, through the same
splice conformance gate as slides and spaces.

WHAT IT DOES. Opens with a starter workbook that demonstrates every column type
it knows, a totals row and a provenance step -- none of which is discoverable
from an empty grid. Sort by clicking a header. Edit a cell by double-clicking.
Import a CSV, by button or by pasting one. Export CSV. Undo. Save, to a real
file, which re-opens with the data in it.

Verified end to end in a browser against the BUILT shell rather than the dev
server: the starter renders, sorting leaves the document untouched and the file
clean, an edit updates the totals row and undo restores both, a semicolon-and-
German-decimals CSV imports with its dates REFUSED and explained, serialize
round-trips to an identical document, and that serialized file boots as a fresh
workbook with both sheets and correct totals.

THE BOOT DISPATCHER is the part worth reading. Only an absent or empty
#bento-doc reaches the starter; everything else refuses, names what it found,
and offers the bytes back untouched -- with no Store, no save handler and no
autosave subscription constructed on that path, so nothing downstream CAN
serialize over somebody's data. It also tells apart the case the kernel cannot:
readEmbeddedDoc returns `text || null`, so a present-but-unreadable block
arrives looking identical to an absent one, and only the boot site can still
see the DOM to know the difference.

AUTOSAVE IS GUARDED by isEncryptionActive() -- the rule the kernel states in
its own header, enforces nowhere, and which spaces' M0 therefore missed
(raised on #226).

TWO LAYOUT BUGS, both found by looking rather than by types:

- The first two rows were hidden behind the header. `position: sticky` resolves
  against the scroll container, so absolutely-positioned rows at top:0 landed
  underneath it. Header and totals are now in normal flow with only the row
  region absolute.
- The findings banner kept a visible strip of its background when empty,
  because `display: grid` beats the [hidden] attribute's own display:none.

Neither is expressible in a test that does not render.

The grid is WINDOWED -- 100k x 6 would be 600,000 nodes, and that, not the
arithmetic, is what stops a browser. Sorting goes through store.view(): it
sorts an order vector, never the data, so it takes no checkpoint and does not
dirty the file. Registered in scripts/apps.mjs and built + gated in CI.

Deliberately not here: formulas, charts, collaboration, the vault binding.

description: Bento, the office suite that fits in a file
release_body:
Download the single file below and open it in any modern browser — it's the document, the viewer and the editor in one. Shipped files self-update through the signed release channel.

- **Select several slides in the sidebar and move them together.** ⌘/Ctrl-click
  adds a slide to the selection, ⇧-click selects a range from the current one,
  and dragging any selected slide moves the whole selection as a block, in its
  order, as one undoable step; Delete removes the selection with the usual
  warning about states and links. A slide's interactive states now travel with
  it when it is dragged — before this a moved slide left its states behind,
  nested under whatever slide was now before them. Asked for in discussion
  #514.

release_body:
A patch release that puts Apple Silicon GPUs to work, adds a Turkish translation of the documentation, and clears CI maintenance gathered since `0.12.2`.

### 🐛 Fixes

- **Apple MPS is now detected for device selection and postprocessing** ([#1408](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1408)). `select_device()` only looked for CUDA, so macOS users fell back to CPU even with a working Metal backend. Automatic selection is now CUDA -> MPS -> CPU, and the `torchvision` postprocessing backend is picked when either GPU is present. Detection goes through `torch.backends.mps.is_available()`, which exists on every supported torch version and reports `False` on non-Apple builds.
- **`threading.currentThread()` replaced with `current_thread()`** ([#1392](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1392)), removing a `DeprecationWarning` on newer Python versions.

### 📚 Documentation

- **Turkish translation** of the documentation, with a build step and `zensical` configuration to match ([#1401](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1401), [#1402](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1402), [#1404](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1404)).
- Multilingual subpath links now resolve correctly ([#1403](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1403)).
- Backend documentation lists MPS alongside CUDA ([#1410](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1410)).

### 🧹 Maintenance & CI

- Device selection and postprocessing backend resolution are covered by tests ([#1409](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1409)).
- Bumped `astral-sh/setup-uv` 8.3.2 → 9.0.0 ([#1399](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1399)), `actions/setup-python` 6.3.0 → 7.0.0 ([#1400](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1400)) and `actions/checkout` 7.0.0 -> 7.0.1 ([#1398](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1398)).
- Relaxed the `twine` requirement to `>=5.1.1,<8.0.0` ([#1406](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1406)).

### ⚡ Performance

NMS with the `IOU` metric, best of 5 runs, on an Apple M2 Pro:

| boxes | numpy | numba | torchvision (MPS) |
| ----: | ----: | ----: | ----------------: |
| 100 | 0.14 ms | 0.02 ms | 1.44 ms |
| 500 | 1.53 ms | 0.36 ms | 1.42 ms |
| 1000 | 5.46 ms | 1.40 ms | 1.45 ms |
| 5000 | 81.37 ms | 34.16 ms | 4.05 ms |
| 20000 | 1237.70 ms | 462.56 ms | 11.75 ms |

Below roughly 500 boxes `numba` stays ahead, but the difference there is about a milliseconds.

**Full Changelog**:
<https://github.com/obss/sahi/compare/0.12.2...0.12.3>

A patch release that fixes the `sahi` command line interface, which was broken on any installation that did not already have `matplotlib` present.

### 🐛 Fixes

- **`matplotlib` is now a declared dependency** ([#1414](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1414)). `sahi.cli` imports `sahi.scripts.coco_error_analysis`, which imports `matplotlib` at module level, but `matplotlib` was never listed in `[project].dependencies` or in any extra. Because the import is eager, every `sahi` command failed on a clean install, including ones unrelated to plotting such as `sahi version`:

  ```
  $ sahi version
    File ".../sahi/cli.py", line 9, in <module>
      from sahi.scripts.coco_error_analysis import analyse
    File ".../sahi/scripts/coco_error_analysis.py", line 13, in <module>
      import matplotlib
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'matplotlib'
  ```

release_body:
A patch release that adds an optional ultrafast-pycocotools backend to COCO evaluation, fixes four crashes and miscounts in COCO and video utilities, speeds up postprocessing and sliced prediction, and raises the torch floor to 2.13.0 on Python 3.10 and newer.

## ✨ Features

- **`sahi coco evaluate` can run on ultrafast-pycocotools** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). Install it with `pip install "sahi[ultrafast]"` and pass `--backend ultrafast` on the CLI or `backend="ultrafast"` to `sahi.scripts.coco_evaluation.evaluate`. pycocotools stays the default, and the tests check that both backends return the same bbox and segm results (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1457).

## 🐛 Fixes

- **COCO evaluation accepts a list of IoU thresholds** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). Passing `iou_thrs` as a list stopped in the summary step with a NumPy "nonzero on 0d arrays" error. Thresholds are now always stored as an array.
- **Video prediction counts skipped frames correctly** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1449). The progress bar total only accounted for `frame_skip_interval` while a visual was shown, and the exported video used `fps / frame_skip_interval` instead of `fps / (frame_skip_interval + 1)`, so it played back faster than the source.
- **`remove_invalid_coco_results` skips bboxes that do not have four values** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1455) instead of raising `IndexError`.
- **`get_coco_segmentation_from_obb_points` returns an empty list for empty input** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1456) instead of raising `IndexError`.

## ⚡ Performance

- **NMS and greedy NMM choose the stored-pair path again when boxes are spread out** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1443). Since `0.12.5` they always read rows from the STRtree on demand, which is slower than a stored pair list when boxes are spread out. They now pick the path by crowding the same way NMM does, and the output is unchanged.
- **Streaming postprocessing drops boxes it has finished with** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1426). Settled boxes are removed from later STRtree queries, so crowded inputs query a tree that shrinks as the loop runs.
- **Sliced prediction decodes the source image once** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1445). `get_sliced_prediction` used to decode the file four times. It now reuses the decode that slicing already holds.
- **`slice_image` uses less peak memory** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1421). Local files decode straight to a NumPy array with OpenCV instead of going through Pillow, and `read_image_size` reads the size from the file header without decoding the image. 16-bit files and anything else OpenCV declines use the Pillow path as before.

## 📦 Build

- **The torch floor is 2.13.0 on Python 3.10 and newer** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1440), 2.8.0 on Python 3.9 and 2.4.1 on Python 3.8, the newest release each of them still has wheels for.
- **Development installs pick the torch build that matches the machine** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1446), CUDA or CPU, instead of always CPU.
- **CI tests Python 3.13 and 3.14** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1433).

## 📚 Documentation

- **Documented commands, defaults and examples match the code** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1427, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1452). This includes the `coco evaluate` options, which now list `--type segm`, `--max_detections` and `--backend`.
- **The quick start ends in a prediction, pages link to the next page, and API parameters are shown as tables** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1428, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1429).
- **The docs point at the site they are published on and serve their markdown** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1431), and demo links resolve outside GitHub (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1435).
- **A new notebook measures batched sliced inference speed** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1447) on the machine it runs on and checks that batching does not change the detections.
- **The README install example uses torch 2.13.0 on CUDA 13.0.**
- **General cleanups** (https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1430, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1436, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1441, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1442, https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1444): notebook outputs are stripped, autoref warnings and dead links are fixed, and punctuation is consistent.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/obss/sahi/compare/0.12.6...0.12.7

description: Framework agnostic sliced/tiled inference + interactive ui + error analysis plots
release_body:
A patch release that adds LibreYOLO as a detection backend, fixes seven bugs in COCO category remapping, slicing, mask conversion and box merging, and builds boolean masks faster.

### ✨ Features

- **LibreYOLO detection backend** ([#1425](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1425)). Install it with `pip install libreyolo` and load MIT-licensed LibreYOLO models with `model_type="libreyolo"`. It reuses the Ultralytics wrapper, and the models guide covers it in every language ([#1467](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1467)).

### 🐛 Fixes

- **Sliced annotations that touch the slice border are kept** ([#1462](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1462)). When a polygon edge lay exactly on a slice border, the intersection came back as a mix of polygons and lines and the annotation was dropped with area 0. The polygon parts are now kept.
- **NMM merges boxes whose overlap equals the match threshold** ([#1464](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1464)). These boxes were claimed by the keeper but never merged, so they disappeared from the output and the keeper box did not grow.
- **`get_bool_mask_from_coco_segmentation` returns a boolean array** ([#1463](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1463)). It returned the float64 canvas, so `Mask.bool_mask` could not be used to index an image.
- **Category remapping maps each id once** ([#1465](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1465)). With `remapping_dict={0: 1, 1: 2}` both categories ended up with id 2 and loading failed with `KeyError`.
- **Subsampled, upsampled, area filtered and bbox clipped Coco objects keep their categories** ([#1466](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1466)). They applied `remapping_dict` a second time to ids that were already remapped, which also affected `clip_bboxes_to_img_dims=True`.
- **Class-aware NMM and greedy NMM accept an image with no detections** ([#1470](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1470)) instead of raising `AttributeError`.
- **`fix_shift_amount_list` and `fix_full_shape_list` accept empty lists** ([#1459](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1459)) instead of raising `IndexError`.

### ⚡ Performance

- **Boolean masks from COCO polygons build about 8x faster** ([#1463](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1463)). The mask is drawn on a uint8 canvas instead of float64, which takes a 1080p mask from 1.03 ms to 0.13 ms on an Intel Core i7-13850HX and uses 8x less memory.

### 📚 Documentation

- **The Chinese and Turkish docs match the English docs again** ([#1461](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1461)).
- **The RT-DETR guide uses the Ultralytics weights the backend loads** ([#1467](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1467)), and the `coco slice` CLI docs no longer list a `--backend` option it does not have ([#1460](https://github.com/obss/sahi/pull/1460)).

release_body:
## wakaru v1.1.0

**Async/generator recovery, esbuild unpacking, better correctness.**

### Highlights

- **Babel async & generators** — `regeneratorRuntime` and `_asyncToGenerator` are restored back to native `async/await` and `function*`
- **esbuild unpacking** — scope-hoisted esbuild bundles are split into proper ES modules
- **Babel 7.24+ classes** — `_callSuper` and single-arg `_createClass` recovered correctly
- **Diagnostics** — opt-in structured warnings and TDZ violation reporting
- **Sentry component names** — recovered from `data-sentry-component` attributes
- **25 correctness fixes** — var/const scoping, duplicate imports, lexical `this`, unresolved marks, and more
- **Fat LTO builds** — smaller and faster binaries
- **Linux ARM64** — native release binaries

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

[{"sha": "043997d0bc58758c4cc81f46bbff038056b58c2e", "author_date": "2026-05-16T14:29:21Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-16T17:19:37Z", "message": "feat(core): synthesize import/export for esbuild scope-hoisted modules

The esbuild scope-hoisted module extractor correctly identified module
boundaries via the `var NS = {}; __export(NS, {...})` pattern but
emitted raw code without import/export statements.  Cross-module
references (which the bundler resolved via direct bindings in the
shared scope) were left as dangling free variables.

Restructure `extract_scope_hoisted_modules` into a two-pass approach:

Pass 1 — collect per-module metadata: declared bindings, referenced
bindings, and exported atoms from the __export registration call.

Pass 2 — emit each module with synthesized ES imports for cross-module
references and exports promoted from the __export binding map.

Additional fixes folded in:

- Case-insensitive filename dedup via a shared `dedup_filename` probe
  loop (try `{base}.js`, `{base}_2.js`, …) matching the CLI's
  `deduplicate_path` logic.  Factory filenames are deduped first, then
  seeded into the same set so scope-hoisted names never collide.

- Consumed namespace decls and __export calls are restored into the
  entry when the entry still references the namespace binding (e.g.
  `export { math_exports as math }`), with imports for the individual
  bindings so the __export getters resolve correctly.

- Effective export sets are expanded beyond T8-registered public API to
  include any declared binding referenced from another module or the
  entry, since the bundler's scope hoisting lets private helpers be
  called across boundaries.

On the claude-code fixture: 340 scope-hoisted modules gain exports,
333 gain imports, and 0 import targets point at missing files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/043997d0bc58758c4cc81f46bbff038056b58c2e"}, {"sha": "06785fd160052e87b2e6fb482f8b296d208f159c", "author_date": "2026-05-11T20:41:13Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:12Z", "message": "fix(core): bound synthetic name search", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/06785fd160052e87b2e6fb482f8b296d208f159c"}, {"sha": "06fcbdd4276e280454f89734d1825d59713ab9e2", "author_date": "2026-05-17T18:36:34Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-17T18:45:56Z", "message": "fix(unpack): merge esbuild init factories into their target module

When a factory module (lazy init wrapped in `y(...)`) only assigns to
bindings belonging to a single scope-hoisted module, merge its body
into that module instead of emitting a separate file with invalid ESM
(imports are read-only, so `import {x} ...; x = ...` would fail).

Also synthesizes imports for cross-module reads in merged bodies,
detects UpdateExpr (count++) as writes, and skips bindings the target
module already imports to avoid duplicate declarations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/06fcbdd4276e280454f89734d1825d59713ab9e2"}, {"sha": "075e06e2545e1a976246a4a8ba24d77689237ae7", "author_date": "2026-05-13T18:01:27Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:13Z", "message": "fix(core): avoid invalid JSX attr renames", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/075e06e2545e1a976246a4a8ba24d77689237ae7"}, {"sha": "087f9b852dcb5ad2b4b2712d618d0973c3074d40", "author_date": "2026-05-11T16:21:29Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-11T20:17:05Z", "message": "feat: hoist embedded require() calls in un_esm pre-pass

Add a pre-pass to un_esm that hoists require() calls out of complex
expressions (sequence expressions, inline conditional interops) into
standalone statements that the existing classification logic can
convert to ES imports.

Handles three patterns:
- export default (i = require("./a"), require("./b"), expr)
  → import i from "./a"; import "./b"; export default expr;
- const a = (i = require("./x")) && i.__esModule ? i : {default: i}
  → import i from "./x"; const a = i;
- export default require("./f")(args)
  → import _default from "./f"; export default _default(args);

Reduces remaining require() calls in real-world-1 from 38 to 4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/1d1b2d728766792da9ade15dc32bcd475212a4cc"}, {"sha": "26879c31ffaef764170d0bc00026759b0a028757", "author_date": "2026-05-17T17:28:31Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-17T17:32:49Z", "message": "fix(core): synthesize imports in esbuild factory modules for scope-hoisted refs

Factory modules extracted by the esbuild unpacker had no import/export
links for cross-module references. When a factory's body referenced a
binding declared in a scope-hoisted module, that reference was invisible
to the scope-hoisted extraction because factory bodies were already
removed from the entry items. This caused scope-hoisted modules to not
export private helpers that factories need, leaving dangling free
variables that DCE would then incorrectly remove.

Restructure the esbuild unpack flow:
- Phase 3 now defers factory emission and collects referenced bindings
  from the resolved AST
- Phase 5 accepts factory refs, expands scope-hoisted exports, and
  returns a binding→filename map
- New Phase 6 emits factories with synthesized import statements
- Factory-referenced namespace bindings map to entry.js with synthesized
  exports when the entry doesn't already export them
- Relative import paths are computed correctly for subdirectory factories
- Private helpers only referenced by factories are absorbed into the
  last scope-hoisted module via expanded find_last_module_end

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/26879c31ffaef764170d0bc00026759b0a028757"}, {"sha": "2bb34bf655c919c1800bc3d4d6455f95ac7c835f", "author_date": "2026-05-17T07:38:36Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-17T08:24:37Z", "message": "refactor(core): extract shared decl_utils module to deduplicate pattern-walking

Five files had near-identical collect_decl_*/collect_pat_* functions for
gathering binding names from declarations and patterns. Consolidate them
into a single decl_utils module that delegates to SWC's find_pat_ids,
which correctly handles all destructuring forms and skips expressions.

Resolves cargo audit warning for transitive rand 0.8.5 dependency.
No breaking API changes; all tests pass with no code modifications.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/2e11c699223eea0d84cbadc2ed545cf910cb6f5e"}, {"sha": "31772bce6d5ba837122f0f4b162eec9f851a591e", "author_date": "2026-05-11T19:35:07Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:12Z", "message": "docs: improve documents", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/31772bce6d5ba837122f0f4b162eec9f851a591e"}, {"sha": "33f8867cfc70354dbab3f95e274f744d3e9c8e2b", "author_date": "2026-05-11T20:38:40Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:12Z", "message": "fix(core): avoid panic in prototype class builder", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/33f8867cfc70354dbab3f95e274f744d3e9c8e2b"}, {"sha": "34b3166c46220ad92739674f8a3ecd8716c2a2dd", "author_date": "2026-05-13T19:03:58Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:13Z", "message": "feat(core): surface structured warnings from best-effort unpack

unpack/unpack_raw now return UnpackOutput with structured
UnpackWarning { filename, kind, message } instead of plain strings.
Parse failures in extracted modules are preserved as raw code and
reported via warnings rather than silently swallowed.

CLI: print warnings to stderr; suppress progress in non-TTY.
WASM: unpack returns { modules, warnings } with typed WakaruWarning.
Tests: integration tests assert no unexpected warnings.", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/34b3166c46220ad92739674f8a3ecd8716c2a2dd"}, {"sha": "368235bdee295ed27c9f04f726878be11032d028", "author_date": "2026-05-11T20:15:47Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:12Z", "message": "fix(core): preserve argument copy loops in arg_rest", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/368235bdee295ed27c9f04f726878be11032d028"}, {"sha": "3813d793d45843712e987ecd9337c64693e3b680", "author_date": "2026-05-17T07:05:16Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-17T07:05:16Z", "message": "feat(core): handle Babel 7.24+ _callSuper and 1-arg _createClass in un_es6_class

The IIFE class pattern with `return _createClass(Foo)` (1 arg, no methods)
was not recognized because try_parse_create_class required >= 2 args.
Additionally, `_callSuper(this, Foo, arguments)` (Babel 7.24+ super helper)
had no rewriting support anywhere in the codebase.

Changes:
- Allow 1-arg _createClass in return statements (seals prototype, no methods)
- Add body-shape detection for _callSuper to babel_helper_utils (Inherits and
  CallSuper variants in BabelHelperKind)
- Detect by: 2-3 params, <=3 stmts, 3-arg Reflect.construct + param2.apply(param1)
- Add CallSuperRewriter to transform safe call sites to super(...)
- Bail class conversion entirely when third arg is unsafe (not `arguments`
  or array literal) to avoid dangling inner-binding references
- Remove orphaned _inherits and _callSuper fn declarations after conversion
- Move is_inherits_fn to babel_helper_utils (drops unresolved_mark, uses
  simple Object name check consistent with existing patterns)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/3813d793d45843712e987ecd9337c64693e3b680"}, {"sha": "39045808cc5a917233f7932eeaa6030f512ca48b", "author_date": "2026-05-16T17:52:58Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-16T17:52:58Z", "message": "refactor(core): extract expr_utils, enforce unresolved_mark, adopt ExprFactory

Consolidates duplicate exprs_structurally_equal / is_undefined helpers
into a shared expr_utils module. Threads unresolved_mark through
UnArgumentSpread, UnNullishCoalescing, UnOptionalChaining, and RemoveVoid
so that `undefined` identifiers are only matched when they refer to the
true global. Also adopts ExprFactory::make_bin() in exponent,
un_conditionals, un_template_literal, and un_nullish_coalescing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/39045808cc5a917233f7932eeaa6030f512ca48b"}, {"sha": "3b6908635a78cc9e423480eaa4641e1b9b163a8b", "author_date": "2026-05-15T19:14:07Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-16T17:03:19Z", "message": "refactor(core): disable DCE by default in decompile pipeline

DeadImports/DeadDecls no longer run in the default pipeline.
A decompiler should preserve the original code faithfully — if a
helper remains after transformation, that is a rule bug to fix,
not something to silently clean up.

Callers that explicitly need DCE can still opt in via
dead_code_elimination: true. The dead_decls and dead_imports test
suites now do this.

Updated test expectations: helper leftovers that DCE was silently
removing now appear in output. Tests assert rule-specific behavior
rather than relying on downstream cleanup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/3b6908635a78cc9e423480eaa4641e1b9b163a8b"}, {"sha": "3c7426aa509859d3768b1b967e7088cbd6a5f7c0", "author_date": "2026-05-17T17:12:09Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-17T17:12:09Z", "message": "fix(core): add ImportDedup to standard pipeline to merge duplicate imports

ImportDedup previously only ran in the sourcemap-enhanced path. Scope-hoisted
bundles produce multiple import statements for the same specifier from the same
module (e.g. `import { randomUUID as x } from "crypto"` repeated 3 times).
Without dedup, UnImportRename generates unnecessary suffixed names (randomUUID_1,
randomUUID_2). Also adds a merge pass that consolidates separate imports from the
same source into a single statement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/3c7426aa509859d3768b1b967e7088cbd6a5f7c0"}, {"sha": "455706aa3f07b4c1ed4460476a4de6e561ddc3fa", "author_date": "2026-05-11T20:36:10Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:12Z", "message": "fix(core): propagate unpack module errors", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/455706aa3f07b4c1ed4460476a4de6e561ddc3fa"}, {"sha": "49f904873629c47b0edfba59771e0f39482a8829", "author_date": "2026-05-13T16:47:45Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-14T17:10:13Z", "message": "fix(core): distinguish bundle parse failures", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/49f904873629c47b0edfba59771e0f39482a8829"}, {"sha": "4aa98b8904f4c93f6ff72e44814c2ea9ca8f6088", "author_date": "2026-05-16T17:53:21Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-16T17:53:21Z", "message": "fix(core): thread unresolved_mark into smart_rename and un_es6_class

SmartRename now verifies `Symbol` is the global binding before renaming
Symbol.for() constants. UnEs6Class now verifies `Object` is the global
binding before matching Object.create/defineProperty patterns in class
inheritance detection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", "html_url": "https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/commit/4aa98b8904f4c93f6ff72e44814c2ea9ca8f6088"}, {"sha": "4bd67923c8f0b4329fb882f7046cf570c85ded2a", "author_date": "2026-05-16T17:53:13Z", "committer_date": "2026-05-16T17:53:13Z", "message": "refactor(core): adopt ExprFactory helpers (.as_callee(), .as_arg())

Replace manual `Callee::Expr(Box::new(...))` and

description: 🔪📦 Javascript decompiler for modern frontend
release_body:
The headline of this release is **experimental Vue 3 SFC recovery** — wakaru can now reconstruct `.vue`-style single-file components from compiled render modules. It's backed by a big wave of correctness fixes that make the everyday decompile path safer, plus new execution-equivalence testing that verifies recovered code actually *runs* the same as the original.

## ✨ Experimental: Vue 3 SFC recovery (`--vue-sfc`)

```bash
wakaru bundle.js --unpack --vue-sfc -o out/
```

wakaru can now recover template-shaped SFC artifacts from compiled Vue 3 render code across **webpack, Vite, and SystemJS** outputs. It reconstructs templates, components and slots, directives (`v-model`, `v-for`, `v-html`, `v-memo`, event handlers with modifiers), conditional branches, and setup-block bindings — and there's a live Vue SFC preview in the playground now too.

This is experimental and there are still gaps, but it already handles a wide range of real-world compiler output.

## 🚀 New recovery

- **Nullish assignment** (`??=`) recovery.
- Expanded AMD and repro-edge recovery.

## 🛡️ Correctness & semantics

A large set of fixes to guarantee decompiled output preserves the original program's behavior:

- **`const` vs `let`** — no longer emits `const` for bindings that are later reassigned (avoids runtime `TypeError`s): mutated IIFE args/loop targets, wrapped binding writes, and mutable destructuring are all preserved as mutable.
- **Object rest & destructuring** — correct recovery of computed object-rest keys, computed parameter destructuring, and adjacent-pick requirements; preserves rest semantics.
- **IIFE & eval** — preserves IIFE and method shapes around `eval` and duplicate parameters; tighter arrow eval scope guards.
- **esbuild / TS helpers** — tightened mangled spread matching, gated object-alias detection, and cleanup of consumed TS helpers.
- **DCE safety** — preserves TDZ reads, deferred lexical reads, observable no-op reads, and import-link checks during transform-only DCE.
- **Misc** — signed numeric `switch` cases.

## 🧪 Testing & CI

  takes &Ident. A nested local reusing a setup binding's minified name now
  falls out via context mismatch rather than a shadow frame.

Every UnpackedModule now records the byte ranges in the original input it
was extracted from (source_ranges) and which input file those refer to
(source_input, filled by the driver for multi-source unpacks):

- esbuild factories: the factory var declarator span
- esbuild/Bun scope-hoisted modules: coalesced body item spans
- webpack4/5: factory function / body statement spans

which writes provenance.json ({module file -> {input, ranges}}) next to
the unpacked modules, using final on-disk names after CLI-side dedup.

Two review findings against the mangled esbuild machinery:

carry the alias preamble and still define a user descriptor-copy utility

minification because the values helper body calls it.

unused Object alias in the module and ran whenever any spread/rest helper
fired, so recovering an unrelated Babel helper deleted stray aliases that
were never part of an esbuild preamble. Both sweeps are now gated on
esbuild-specific evidence (matched mangled helpers, __defNormalProp, or
inline esbuild spread calls).

description: 🔪📦 Javascript decompiler for modern frontend
release_body:
This release has two headliners: **Bun single-file executable extraction** — point wakaru at a `bun build --compile` binary and it unpacks the JavaScript inside — and **Closure Compiler output recovery**. Previous releases only understood Closure's ModuleManager bundle format; wakaru now also recovers the code patterns Closure Compiler itself emits. Alongside them: webpack 5 detection handles bundles with no IIFE wrapper and array-form module tables, and the public Rust API on crates.io was redesigned.

## 🧊 Bun single-file executables

```bash
wakaru ./compiled-app --unpack -o out/          # decompile the embedded JS
wakaru bun extract ./compiled-app -o extracted/ # dump every embedded file
```

- `--unpack` accepts a Bun single-file executable (`bun build --compile` output — PE, Mach-O, or ELF): wakaru validates Bun's embedded module graph, selects the JS/JSX/TS/TSX entries, and sends them through the same unpack pipeline as ordinary bundles.
- `wakaru bun extract` writes **every** embedded file record — JavaScript, assets, binaries — under `extracted/files/`, with a `manifest.json` mapping original Bun paths to safe output paths. Extraction only writes files; it never executes or trusts their contents.
- Both the Bun 1.3.3–1.3.8 and the 1.3.9+ container record layouts are supported, and extraction memory usage was cut by reducing AST retention during factory extraction.

## 📦 Webpack detection, expanded

- **Bundles without an IIFE wrapper** — modern webpack 5 output that inlines the runtime at top level is now detected and split, including extraction of the inline startup section as a proper entry module and entries with no `exports` anchor.
- **Array-form module containers** (`webpack_modules` as an array) are now unpacked (#200), and minified entry loaders survive splitting.
- HMR-style factory indirection, eager `import()` startups, Terser-merged statement sequences, and entry-owned runtime mutations are all handled; webpack 4 gains concat-offset and parenthesized-factory recovery.
- New `--unpack=inspect` profile keeps finer module boundaries for static inspection of scope-hoisted output.
- Multi-input unpacks now keep **stable public module paths**: sibling imports resolve to the right file instead of depending on argument order, and imports are rewritten after output-filename dedup.
- A new emitted-module graph validator checks every unpack result for dangling imports and unparseable output as part of diagnostics.

## 🚀 New recovery

- **Closure Compiler patterns** — wakaru now recovers `for...of` loops from Closure's `$jscomp.makeIterator` lowering and ES6 classes from its prototype-based class output, gated on the Closure runtime bootstrap so ordinary code is untouched. Recovery is verified by *executing* the recovered classes against the originals across multiple Closure Compiler versions.
- Object literals are rebuilt from Babel's loose-mode computed-property assignments.
- Optional chains rooted at parameters are recovered.
- Inline export declarations from scope-hoisted bundles are adopted directly.

## 🛡️ Correctness & semantics

- **Class recovery got a safety pass**: functions whose identity or construction behavior matters — `new.target` users, `Reflect.construct` newTargets, constructor-sensitive values flowing through aliases, prototypes with dynamic key order, reused `var` class bindings, default-exported constructors relying on hoisting, evaluated export initializers, duplicate sloppy-mode params — are now preserved instead of converted.
- **JSX survives renaming**: export renames can no longer lowercase a component tag into a DOM element, capitalized aliases survive import renaming, and `createElement` calls in optional-call, paren-wrapped, callee, and member-object positions are guarded.
- Reserved words in decomposed imports and export locals are aliased instead of emitted verbatim; regenerator decoding rolls back cleanly on unsupported shapes; sloppy-mode output is verified as script, not module.

## 🦀 Public Rust API, redesigned

The `wakaru` crate now exposes a compiler-style service: `decompile(Source, DecompileOptions)` and `unpack(Vec<Source>, UnpackOptions)` (plus incremental `UnpackJob`), with structured diagnostics, provenance, and detection reports instead of warning strings — and `bun` / `debug` namespaces for standalone extraction and rule tracing. `wakaru-core` is published in lockstep as an implementation detail; the façade is the supported surface (`cargo doc -p wakaru` is the contract).

## 📦 npm

`npx wakaru` now works — the bare `wakaru` package is an alias for `@wakaru/cli`, pinned to the same version.

## ⚡ Performance

Scope-hoisted splitting indexes cross-cluster symbols instead of rescanning, and export-rename shadow analysis is batched.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.8.0...v1.9.0

description: 🔪📦 Javascript decompiler for modern frontend
release_body:
v1.10.0 is a correctness release: 95 fixes, no new bundler formats. Most of the work went into two areas — **SystemJS modules now decompile to real ESM exports** in many more shapes, and **CommonJS `.default` interop is recovered** behind cross-module proofs that fail closed. Also new: `wakaru debug validate` reports source locations and flags CommonJS residuals.

## 🔗 SystemJS exports, reconstructed

- Exports written through `_export` in assignment, `var`-initializer, sequence, and expression forms are reconstructed into ESM export declarations instead of surviving as runtime calls.
- Setter re-exports are recovered: live setter re-exports no longer synthesize fake locals, arbitrary and named-object setter re-export shapes are reconstructed, and re-export names are preserved exactly.
- `System.register` modules whose `declare` takes no export parameter are reconstructed; unreadable `declare` parameters fail closed instead of guessing.
- Every export emission path now proves the target name is free before binding an export directly; unrepresentable export names take the shared alias path, and function-callee IIFEs are parenthesized on every emit path.
- Export sequence semantics, default-export expression context, chained exports (which now reuse live bindings), and IIFE exports preceding member assignments are all preserved.

## 🎛️ CommonJS interop, proven then recovered

- Default-only providers, coupled lazy defaults, and exact ordered `Object.assign` copy shells are proven at the multi-module fact barrier and recovered — mixed surfaces, unresolved providers, extra runtime behavior, and cycles fail closed.
- Proven CommonJS self reads, property imports, object imports, callable property imports, and named-only provider imports are repaired into direct ESM references.
- CommonJS export-star loops are recovered, defaults are recovered from export getter maps, and default-compat postambles are matched in logical form and dropped when proven dead.
- The proofs fail closed on direct `eval` reads, compound writes and optional chains, prototype-mutating members (`__proto__`, `__defineGetter__`, `__defineSetter__`), conditional callable exports, residual requires, and mid-body directives — `exports.__proto__ = value` stays an honest residual instead of becoming a fabricated named export.
- Webpack inner-UMD wrappers: proven defaults are recovered, inner exports must be unconditional, and deferred rewrites are rejected.

## 🚀 New recovery

- **Minified TypeScript CJS enums**: the collapsed `(exports.X || (exports.X = {}))` enum IIFE is proven literal-only and recovered as an exported enum object — with the reserved-name, deferred-read, `eval`, and binding-grammar holes closed and each rejected shape covered by tests.
- Called module-export assignments are lowered through receiver chains, chained local default exports are split, and default exports are recovered from `var` initializers.

## 🧭 Validation & diagnostics

- `wakaru debug validate` findings now carry source locations — `filename:line:column` in human output, one-based `line`/`column` fields in `--json`.
- The validator reports CommonJS residuals: unresolved `module` / `exports` runtime uses left in files that contain ESM syntax (direct safe `typeof` probes excluded).
- Import-backed local re-exports resolve to their origin, ambiguous star exports are detected, duplicate export declarations are pinpointed, reported import cycles carry a real cycle witness, and repeated parser recovery warnings are coalesced.
- With `--unpack=inspect` and `--provenance`, fine modules split from one oversized write component carry optional `context_ranges` identifying the coarse evidence-pooling context in the original input.

## 📦 Webpack

- CSS runtime modules: runtime metadata is recovered and emitted CSS adapter forms are handled.
- Reused loader and runtime parameters are localized per factory, unsafe loader reuse is isolated, and reuse normalization is gated by alias lifetime.
- String module IDs now emit JavaScript filenames: non-JS resource IDs append `.js` (`src/style.less` → `src/style.less.js`), loader queries and URL fragments are stripped from filesystem names, and collisions get stable suffixes.
- Identity substitution requires a stable module surface, the guarded global fallback is hardened, generated global injection is recovered, empty-factory default exports are restored, and wrapper lifting respects class execution contexts.

## 🛡️ Rename & binding safety

- A capture sweep across the rename rules: parameter defaults, named exports, alias recovery, value renames, and namespace aliases can no longer be captured by inner scopes or globals, and parameter-default binding order is preserved.
- The shared rename shadow index now fails closed (and trips a debug assertion) when queried about a binding it never analyzed, and JSX intrinsic-tag checks use ASCII lowercase — matching the `/^[a-z]/` test JSX transforms actually apply.
- Object-rest synthetic aliases are sanitized for string keys and made collision-free; mutable require locals stay mutable; `const` is recovered after declaration merges; externally used `for...of` loop bindings survive.

## ⚙️ Async, accessors, generators

- Async flattening preserves callable names and renames colliding bindings instead of capturing them.
- Class accessor recovery is verified before conversion, and legacy TypeScript accessor forms are preserved.
- TypeScript async state machines and regenerator decoding preserve state-callback locals.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.9.0...v1.10.0

release_body:
v1.12.0 is a performance release. **Wakaru is now 27–42% faster end-to-end on large bundles.** The rest of the release is correctness work on exports, loops, and esbuild splitting.

## ⚡ Performance

Five changes make up the speedup: 27–29% less end-to-end time on medium bundles and 42% less on a large esbuild bundle, for a few dozen MiB more peak memory.

- The CLI binary uses mimalloc as its global allocator. The `wakaru` crate and the WASM build leave the allocator to their callers.
- Both unpack phases start the largest modules first, so one big module no longer becomes the critical path.
- Rules move statement and argument trees instead of deep-cloning them.
- `UnEsm` checks whether a module has anything to convert before building its binding index.
- Internal binding tables use a faster hasher.

## 🔗 Exports and imports

- CommonJS named exports assigned under conditions become live ESM bindings, and the `exports.x = void 0` sentinels in front of them are dropped.
- Named-export assignment chains are split into one binding per export when their values are stable.
- Module-level copies of named imports are renamed after the import they copy.

## 📦 esbuild splitting

Mutable state written from several esbuild modules is declared once by its owner and imported everywhere else. CommonJS-style factories go through the same path, so their bodies are always emitted.

## 🛡️ Correctness

- For-of recovery keeps `let` when the loop body writes the binding, and leaves loops that write a `const` alone.
- Export aliases stay separate when either side is reassigned.
- Generator recovery matches the state parameter by scope, so a nested callback with the same minified name no longer blocks it.
- `--diagnostics` and `debug validate` report `var` declarations that conflict with `let`, `const`, or `class` in the same scope.

## 🧪 Debug CLI

- `wakaru debug enumerate-chunks` lists the chunk files a bundle would load at runtime, from a static read of one input: webpack lazy chunks and relative `import` / `import()` specifiers. Experimental, see the debug CLI reference.

## 🔧 Dependencies

Bump `swc_core` to 78.0.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/pionxzh/wakaru/compare/v1.11.0...v1.12.0

description: :cookie: A full-featured, hackable tiling window manager written and configured in Python (X11 + Wayland)
release_body:
This release contains a completely rewritten Wayland backend as a python C
module, removing the complex-to-install dependency chain that was
previously required. As a result, the dependencies to run wayland have
completely changed. Of course this new wayland backend is still
experimental, bug reports and patches welcome.

In this release we also add a new maintainer Richard Carnibella @richcarni,
who has done a substantial amount of work to get the new wayland backend
stable for merging and release.

As always, thanks to all the (other) contributors for this release:

This moves all of the non-docs infra to uv, deleting requirements.txt,
requirements-dev.txt, setup.cfg, tox.ini, and dev.sh, each of which had a
slightly different set of dependencies in them, and consolidates to
pyproject.toml to manage all of this.

It also consolidates on using the makefile as the entry point for
everything, and has CI call `make check check-packaging`. There are some
new variables for supplying only a single backend or python version.

As a consequence of using `uv sync --all-extras` for CI, we now need to
install the wayland deps in all environments even if we are only going to
run the x11 backend tests, but that seems simpler than fragmenting these
things again.

Finally, I organized the deps into four sections: dev, optional_core,
widgets, and wayland. I wonder if optional_core is worth it, or if we
should just start requiring all of those? But the other three seem
reasonable to me.

It looks like the uv lock file is expected to be committed based on
https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/9797 , but I generally find these
kinds of lock files annoying, and we haven't needed one in the past. Given
that we should encode any real constraints/bugs we know about (e.g. API
incompatibilities, bugs, etc.) in pyproject.toml directly, I don't see a
ton of value in uv.lock. I think it will also help downstreams to not feel
like they have to package *exactly* the versions we happened to test with,
but can just respect our pyproject.toml.

This commit drops scripts/ffibuild, because over a series of commits
(9770e8c , 24435ad , and 5736f4f ) we removed the need to pre-build ffi
stuff except for wayland, so the script ends up just being a wrapper around
the single ffi build we still needed. There's no real need for it, we can
just call that build script directly.

After the conversion of GenPollCommand to asyncio.create_subprocess_* I
have a lot of:

    Unknown child process pid 1312154, will report returncode 255

from qtile's stderr in my xsession logs. It turns out that this is from
asyncio [1] who is confused because our SIGCHILD handler wait()ed on its
process. So let's do the same thing we do for tasks: keep a list of tasks,
and not really wait on those (via WNOWAIT), so that we can leave them for
asyncio so it doesn't get confused.

Much like create task, we need to be careful to use acall_process() vs.
asyncio.create_subprocess_* whenever we want to await on one of these
processes. (Well, not really: acall_process() doesn't return the task's
exit code, so the only consequence of these is that it's slightly annoying
logspam. But in the future if we decided we wanted the exit code from the
acall_process() API, it might be confusing as to why we don't get it.)

[1]: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/5bd4bf04c4ac1ad67760e0b7852a05e796741e6f/Lib/asyncio/unix_events.py#L937-L939

Wayland's implementation is better than x11's since it uses actual WM
semantics, and also it's not generally very backend-specific, so let's
adopt that approach for both backends. We can do this leveraging async so
we don't need to block the rest of the event loop, potentially allowing for
other shutdown code to happen.

There is one insidiously complex change hidden in here, which is the shift
from:

    if not isinstance(win, base.Internal):

to:

    def normal_windows(self) -> list[base.WindowType]:
        return list(
            filter(lambda w: isinstance(w, base.Window), self.windows_map.copy().values())
        )

it turns out our systray is not a base.Internal window, but also does not
set NET_WM_PID, so we were previously not killing it in the x11 version via
get_pid().

However, if you .kill() (i.e. WM_DELETE_WINDOW instead of the kill(2)
syscall) the systray widget's window, the X server kills the connection
that window was created from, which just so happens to be qtile's main
connection, which kills the whole WM.

So instead, we switch to only trying to kill "normal" windows, since those
are the clients with state we want to notify that we're shutting down.

(The systray widget is finalized [or not, modulo bugs :)] via the normal
widget finalize() path.)

Launching programs that read from stdin (e.g. `/bin/cat`) through `lazy.spawncmd()`
completely freezes Qtile, killing the spawned process from the TTY results
in a zombie process, and Qtile remains frozen.

Steps to reproduce:
1. trigger `lazy.spawncmd()` through its assigned keybind
2. run `/bin/cat` using the spawn prompt

The issue is mostly triggered accidentally due to tab-completion, for example:
- `pc` -> `pc1pc1toppm` instead of `pcmanfm`
- `ma` -> `machinectl` instead of `materialgram`
- `t` -> `tabs` instead of `telegram`

The `spawn` function is supposed to redirect standard file descriptors
of the child process to `/dev/null` using dup2, but the order of arguments
is incorrect which is causing it to silently fail.

Swapping `null.fileno()` and `0,1,2` fixes the issue, as the intended behavior
is to duplicate `null.fileno()` to `stdio` and not the other way around.

Related documentation:
* [os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2)
  * (os.POSIX_SPAWN_DUP2, fd, new_fd)
  * Performs os.dup2(fd, new_fd).
* [os.dup2](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.dup2)
  * os.dup2(fd, fd2)
  * Duplicate file descriptor fd to fd2, closing the latter first if necessary.
* [man dup2](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/dup.2.html)
  * int dup2(int oldfd, int newfd);
  * The file descriptor newfd is adjusted so that it now refers to the same open file description as oldfd.

But also, we already have code that spawns qtile, creates processes, etc.
that is complex and does all the multiprocessing stuff for us. Let's just
use it.

In order to do that, we need to explicitly call the ._atexit() handler for
Lifecycle, since it is not registered in our "little qtile" call. Perhaps
we should just switch run_qtile() to write out the config and exec qtile,
so that we get *exactly* the behavior we expect, vs. reimplementing a bunch
of it. But for now, I'll just do this.

with other qtiles in the test suite that ran after it with the
graceful_shutdown() patch. But since this cleanup is a pretty big win, I
didn't look very hard at root causing the problem.

...and drop `qtile udev`. It turns out that some distros (fedora, arch) run
their udev daemon in the initramfs (which makes sense, of course, not sure
why I didn't think of it earlier). That means that in order to run this
code, we'd need to include it in the initramfs, which seems like a pain.

Instead, let's just rearrange the rules to chmod o+w things. This is
simpler for users than having a special group, since groups that exists
across distros are hard (sudo on ubuntu instead of  wheel on fedora, etc.).
Distro packagers can use whatever rules make sense for their distro.

In the rules themselves, the backlight and battery there is just one file
and it seems to exist sysfs symlink time for the device, so we can use a
simple rule.

For the battery charge control, there is two files, so we need to run two
commands (we could use shell globbing here to do one command, but the
quoting is... annoying :).

I tried several different ways to match it at sysfs symlink creation time,
but kept getting:

    BAT0: Process '/usr/bin/chmod o+w /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/charge_control_start_threshold' failed with exit code 1

because the file is only created when the specific driver is loaded. So, we
trigger on that, and hard code the battery path.

All this is to say: I believe this is simpler and easier to use, since it
doesn't require anything in the initramfs or having a specific group hard
coded, even if it is a bit uglier.

python3.14 depreciates event loop policies entirely, in favor of just
manually specifying the event loop as an argument to asyncio.run().

we were really using the event loop policy as a hack for not having a
global variable, so let's switch to a global variable instead, and use it
in the one place we need it.

loop_factory= argument to asyncio:

      File "/home/runner/work/qtile/qtile/libqtile/core/manager.py", line 216, in loop

    TypeError: run() got an unexpected keyword argument 'loop_factory'

but maybe that's ok: 3.10 is outside of our last-three-versions policy, and
3.11 will be outside it in a few months when 3.14 is released.

There is another option here: since the motivation for this was really
#2620, we could "just" switch the battery to running in-loop, which would
mean that it is not run via run_in_executor() i.e. in a separate thread.
That means that get_running_loop() would return the right loop, and we
wouldn't need this hack at all.

(It also means that the battery could potentially block the UI while
reading from e.g. procfs/sysfs files, but that seems unlikely. Perhaps it
also suggests another widget type: something with an `async def poll()`,
which could run in the main loop and avoid both of these problems.)

The only other widget which uses send_notification() is pomodoro, which
doesn't read any files at all and just uses gettimeofday(), which is a VDSO
i.e. memory access, that should also not block, so if we convert the
battery widget, we should do this one as well.

Finally, we suggest use of send_notification() in the hooks documentation,
but all hooks are fired from the main thread, so the get_running_loop()
call should work fine there.

That does mean we'd have to be careful to always send_notification() from
the main thread going forward, but it doesn't seem like that hard of a
challenge.

Qtile's flake no longer provides an overlay (#5420). Updated NixOS
example to set `services.xserver.windowManager.qtile.package` directly
from the flake input. Reworded intro, improved bullet list consistency,
and
added reST `.. note::` disclaimer.

Without these changes, flake users may encounter the following error:

```bash
error: attribute 'overlays' missing
   at /nix/store/.../overlays.nix:3:6:
    2|   nixpkgs.overlays = [
    3|     (inputs.qtile-flake.overlays.default)
```

This can be confusing for those who haven’t seen the recent `flake.nix`
update, especially newcomers to Nix.

**Why this refactor?**
Previously, the flake returned an overlay, which required users to:

1. Create an `overlays.nix` file.
2. Define Qtile’s overlay and import it locally.
3. Understand overlay mechanics — adding extra complexity for those
unfamiliar with them.

By switching to direct package specification, we remove unnecessary
steps and reduce complexity. The new approach is:

* Easier to read and maintain.
* More explicit about which package is used.
* Less work for the end user.

**TL;DR:** Returning an overlay was overkill. Directly defining the

This converts all URL fetching widgets to aiohttp, so that we can make them
"async native" and avoid using more threads.

As a result of this conversion, I had to change around a bunch of the
monkey patching in the tests. Instead of adding more monkey patching, I
switched them to call httpbin, exercising the real http code. Obviously,

release_body:
This is a "fast-follow" release for our new wayc backend. There have been
many bugfixes (thanks to all the reporters and early testers)! We've even
landed a couple fixes for long-time x11 bugs.

Thanks to all the contributors for this release:

    elParaguayo
    Gurjaka
    Kai Stian Olstad
    Michał Górny
    RFCreate
    richcarni
    Tycho Andersen

than try and fix this up, let's just do the same thing wayland does: keep
track of the last window we entered, because that's the one the mouse is
currently over.

Since we're doing the same thing wayland is, we can do it on the core
object, and get rid of some backend specific code for x11 here.

This hopefully:

it's a nice improvement, but I haven't been able to verify yet, nor has
anyone on that bug.

Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/6f0977f2244f234fc2a79f899177af052a6fa914"}, {"sha": "70d732c8e1d87c5d40856d1c1d51f0733db0ddb3", "author_date": "2025-12-06T13:43:32Z", "committer_date": "2025-12-10T03:19:22Z", "message": "test(eval): check for raise exception during eval execution", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/70d732c8e1d87c5d40856d1c1d51f0733db0ddb3"}, {"sha": "75618d3810196a5cdf8a6cf8ed61639bbdfd3100", "author_date": "2025-11-23T04:45:30Z", "committer_date": "2025-11-23T12:04:03Z", "message": "Support building without wayland backend

Support passing `backend=x11` config setting symmetric to
`backend=wayland` that can be used to disable building the Wayland
backend entirely, rather than trying to build it anyway. This is
important for redistributors who need to ensure reproducible build
irrespective of whether Wayland dependencies are installed in the build
environment or not. The automatic behavior is preserved if neither value
is passed.

While at it, I've made the automatic path output the exception message
as well -- it's not exactly helpful when you see a bunch of successful
compilations followed by "Warning: Wayland backend not built. Backend
will not run."

Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/990fe756fdf72ca02403e827d79ab1dfeb7fdfb2"}, {"sha": "9e6f1d6d12013e4d1c71c5333e660c8a1db393f4", "author_date": "2025-12-11T02:26:37Z", "committer_date": "2025-12-13T09:00:47Z", "message": "widgets: separate Volume and PulseVolume

Because PulseVolume inherits from Volume, it also inherits all of the
timers, which means it still runs commands to find the volume, even if it
can get them over the wire from pulse.

Instead, let's hoist the common code (mostly icon resolution, formatting,
and rendering) to VolumeBase, and have each inherit from it with their own
implementation for actually getting the volume.

Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/9e6f1d6d12013e4d1c71c5333e660c8a1db393f4"}, {"sha": "abeba93defb2e7c9fbfbdda9cc4598a2291426f9", "author_date": "2025-12-06T10:59:37Z", "committer_date": "2025-12-08T21:49:22Z", "message": "[wayland] Add idle notify/inhibit support

Adds support for wayland's idle-notify and idle-inhibit extensions.

Inhibitors can be created in a number of ways:

- By the application itself
- In users' configs (via a new idle_inhibitors variable)
- Dynamically (lazy.window.add_idle_inhibitor())
- Globally (lazy.core.set_idle_inhibitor())

Signed-off-by: Tycho Andersen <tycho@tycho.pizza>", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/d5f4e27cf085cb2756bbcac35f6d68c04e11de02"}, {"sha": "ec7fce6a3b6d466689736349c61ff60e21327904", "author_date": "2025-11-19T02:15:39Z", "committer_date": "2025-11-22T22:36:25Z", "message": "bar: preserve bar and widget references during finalization

The core insight here is: finalization is for the resources allocated by a
bar or widget, not deleting the bar or widgets themselves. If we do that,
then when people turn their monitors back on, we will have mutilated their
configs, deleting the bars.

Instead, we should finalize these python objects, since they know how to
re-allocate the resources as necessary on _configure() again if someone
re-attaches a screen. However, we do not do silly things like
widgets.clear() (deleting all the widgets from a bar), or
screen.top = None, removing the widget from the Screen.

This lets us revert 99c8a54b026d ("x11: don't ignore powered off
monitors"), since we really do want to ignore powered off monitors, but we
couldn't before because we were deleting widgets and bars from configs when
the monitors were disconnected.

Move imports out of `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks to real module-level imports
where it doesn't cause circular imports, and drop the accompanying
`from __future__ import annotations` where possible. Forward references to
still-needed TYPE_CHECKING-only imports are preserved, and the few files
that still require them (e.g. for self-referential annotations or known
circular dependencies between backend, config, manager, etc.) keep both
the guard and the future import.

We can remove all of these __future__ and imports and TYPE_CHECKING guards
once our lowest supported python version is 3.14, which imports PEP 649,
deferred evaluation of annotations: https://peps.python.org/pep-0649/

This gets rid of ~300 lines of boilerplate that I often find inscrutable:
"when should I put this in TYPE_CHECKING? when should I not? why the
difference?".

Now that we can use upstream zoneinfo to do lookup-by-string for timezone,
switch to that so there's no longer an optional out of tree dependency
required.

This also greatly simplifies the tests: we don't need any fake bar
infrastructure, monkey patching of all the libraries, etc. We can just
create the widget, set the timezone, and call poll() accordingly to see
what time it renders.

Fixes #5798

When the prompt widget is open, it saves a reference to the current
window. When the widget releases the keyboard, it tries to focus the
previously focused window. If that window has been closed then the
wayland backend tries to focus a view object that has already been freed
in the backend, resulting in a segfault.

The fix is to check whether qtile is still managing the window before
trying to focus it.", "html_url": "https://github.com/qtile/qtile/commit/1d2a25c6ca6be81915567f4126a652bd03ed74eb"}, {"sha": "1f87c443c447cd3447e3b3f99373f5cddf76e25f", "author_date": "2026-04-06T15:41:43Z", "committer_date": "2026-04-06T22:54:19Z", "message": "Fix Volume widget crash on reload

The Volume widget has a background task to check for volume changes.
This task is not cleared when the config is reloaded and so tries to
draw the bar with references to finalised `Drawer` and `TextLayout`
objects.

This PR ensures the task is deleted when the widget is finalised.

This PR adds a `stretch` configuration option which, when set to

`poll` and `apoll` are stub methods intended to be overridden by

it is set to 'line', which is the regular appearance of the cursor.
The other options are 'block', 'none', and 'bar'.
